# Classic recording credits

These files are adapted opening excerpts of published recordings. Audio changes: loudness normalization to a -23 LUFS target, gentle fade-in/out, MP3 64 kbps / 32 kHz encoding; original channel count retained. They are not newly composed or generated music.

The stone track is the full available 29.736-second koto recording; all other excerpts contain 120 seconds of audio. MP3 padding adds around 0.04 seconds.

## Attribution and licenses

## Provenance notes
- License verified on each Wikimedia Commons file description using web search/open, 2026-09-26.
- Clair de lune has separate composition and recording licenses: the composition is public domain, but this recording is CC BY 3.0; do not label it public domain.
- Yangguan Sandie is traditional guqin music, not Mo Li Hua; do not claim the latter. The provided audio adaptation remains CC BY-SA 3.0.
- Sakura Sakura identification is supported by the Commons category; the page describes an unnamed woman playing a 13-string koto. Torsodog is the credited recorder, not a verified performer name. This is a field recording and may contain ambient sound.
- Canon and Gymnopédie are Kevin MacLeod’s published arrangements/recordings; the pages do not establish every instrument’s acoustic versus sampled production.
- The famous status refers to the compositions; these are openly licensed performances, not claimed to be famous commercial master recordings.
- Output is optimized for site payload; it is not lossless/high-fidelity distribution.

---- Original alternatives (tracks 9–16) ----
庭间 · 八首原创空间配乐 / Original arrangements (v20)
Composition, arrangement and digital performance: Tingjian Studio project, 2026.
No third-party melody or commercial recording is reproduced.

Instrument samples: FluidR3 General MIDI soundfont, Frank Wen and contributors;
MIDI.js MP3 conversion distributed by gleitz/midi-js-soundfonts.
Source: https://github.com/gleitz/midi-js-soundfonts/tree/master/FluidR3_GM
License: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 United States
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/us/
Changes: samples sequenced, sustained with crossfades, mixed with original synthesized
percussion, stereo room reflections, fades and loudness normalization.
Samples are used as instruments in these original rendered compositions.
